name: Shelomith
overview: Shelomith was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of Rehoboam and Maacah. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or detailed background provided beyond his lineage. His role is primarily genealogical, linking him to the royal family of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Shelomith is a proper name meaning 'at peace.' There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it reflects a common Hebrew personal name of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Shelomith is explicitly recorded as the son of Rehoboam and Maacah, establishing his place within the Davidic royal line. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond these parents.
scriptureSignificance: Shelomith's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his connection to Rehoboam, the king of Judah, through his parentage. This establishes him as part of the lineage that continued the Davidic dynasty, which is central to God's covenant promises. While the biblical text does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his inclusion underscores the importance of genealogical records in tracing God's providential plan through history.
